les: Van die see tot in die lug en terug
kaps_punt: Die watersiklus: water verdamp, kondenseer, vries en smelt in die watersiklus

items.bewering: Die water op die aarde beweeg heeltyd van die see na die lug en dan na die land. Dieselfde water loop hierdie pad oor en oor, en ons noem dit die watersiklus.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle' (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/evaporation-and-water-cycle): water evaporates from the oceans, and 'only about 10 percent of the water evaporated from the oceans is transported over land and falls as precipitation'; NOAA, 'The water cycle' (https://www.noaa.gov/education/resource-collections/freshwater/water-cycle). There is a real net movement of water from the sea, through the air, to the land, and it keeps repeating, so the sentence is true as a description of the cycle's route. Most water evaporated from the sea rains straight back into the sea, so it does not hold for every drop. The lesson does not say 'all', and NOAA calls the simple circular model a useful one, so this is not a falsehood at Grade 4. Recorded so a person can see it was weighed.

items.bewering: By sommige stappe op hierdie pad verander die water van toestand.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: NOAA, 'The water cycle' (https://www.noaa.gov/education/resource-collections/freshwater/water-cycle): evaporation, condensation, melting and freezing are changes of state within the cycle; the flow of rivers and runoff is not.

items.bewering: Die son se hitte laat die water in die siklus smelt en verdamp.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: NOAA Ocean Today, 'The Water Cycle' (https://oceantoday.noaa.gov/watercycle/): energy from the sun causes surface water to evaporate; NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory student sheet (https://gml.noaa.gov/outreach/info_activities/pdfs/CTA_the_water_cycle.pdf): liquid water forms when winter ice and snow melt. NOAA JetStream notes that the energy can also come from the air or the ground, but these are ultimately warmed by the sun, so the sentence holds.

items.bewering: Water wat weer hitte verloor, kondenseer en vries op ander plekke in die siklus.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: Britannica, 'Phase change' (https://www.britannica.com/science/phase-change): freezing and condensation release energy (latent heat), so they happen when the water gives off heat; USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': 'Condensation occurs when saturated air is cooled.'

items.bewering: Die son se hitte en die warm lug dra die water boontoe.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: Met Office, 'What are clouds and how do they form?' (https://weather.metoffice.gov.uk/learn-about/weather/types-of-weather/clouds/what-are-clouds-and-how-do-they-form): water vapour rises with the air, and the air cools as it rises. Checked the picture of the air 'carrying' the water: rising warm air carries the invisible water vapour upwards, and the sun's heat is what makes the vapour and warms the air. The picture holds and does not lead a learner anywhere false.

items.bewering: Swaartekrag trek die water weer af na 'n laer plek.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: NOAA GML student sheet (https://gml.noaa.gov/outreach/info_activities/pdfs/CTA_the_water_cycle.pdf): runoff 'flows downhill under the influence of gravity'; NASA GPM 'Exploring the Water Cycle' teacher's guide (https://gpm.nasa.gov/education/sites/default/files/lesson_plan_files/exploring-water-cycle/Exploring%20the%20Water%20Cycle%20TG.pdf): gravity makes precipitation fall and water flow downward over the land.

items.bewering: Die son skyn op die see en op die water in damme en riviere. Die son se hitte maak daardie water warmer, en 'n deel daarvan verdamp. Dit gaan as waterdamp die lug in.
items.blok: Die son laat die water verdamp
items.bron: USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': evaporation changes liquid water to water vapour, it is driven by heat, and it happens from oceans, seas, lakes and rivers; NOAA Ocean Today: energy from the sun evaporates surface water into water vapour.

items.bewering: Waterdamp is water as 'n gas, en jy kan dit glad nie sien nie.
items.blok: Die son laat die water verdamp
items.bron: Met Office, 'What are clouds and how do they form?': water vapour is an invisible gas, and clouds can only be seen because the vapour has condensed into droplets.

items.bewering: Water verdamp ook van nat grond en van nat klere op die lyn.
items.blok: Die son laat die water verdamp
items.bron: USGS, 'Evapotranspiration and the Water Cycle' (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/evapotranspiration-and-water-cycle): water evaporates into the air from the soil surface; USGS glossary of water cycle terms (https://www.usgs.gov/glossary/glossary-water-cycle-terms): evaporation is liquid water changing to water vapour, driven by heat. Washing drying on the line is the same process.

items.bewering: Hoe warmer die dag is, hoe vinniger verdamp die water.
items.blok: Die son laat die water verdamp
items.bron: USGS circular (https://pubs.usgs.gov/unnumbered/70046398/report.pdf): the rate of evaporation varies with the temperature of the water, the wind and the dryness of the air; USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': evaporation is much slower near freezing point than near boiling point. Wind and humidity also play a part, but the comparison as stated, warmer means faster with everything else equal, is true.

items.bewering: Die waterdamp beweeg saam met die lug hoër op. Hoër op is die lug baie kouer as naby die grond.
items.blok: Hoër op kondenseer die waterdamp
items.bron: NOAA JetStream, 'Layers of the Atmosphere' (https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/atmosphere/layers-of-atmosphere): in the troposphere the temperature falls with height, from about 17 °C on average at the surface to about -51 °C at the tropopause; Met Office: rising air cools. At cloud height the air is typically several to tens of degrees colder, so 'baie kouer' holds.

items.bewering: Die waterdamp koel daar af en kondenseer weer tot klein druppels water.
items.blok: Hoër op kondenseer die waterdamp
items.bron: Met Office, 'What are clouds and how do they form?': the vapour cools and condenses into tiny liquid droplets, about a hundredth of a millimetre across; USGS: 'Condensation occurs when saturated air is cooled.' 'weer' is right because the vapour came from liquid water.

items.bewering: 'n Wolk is nie waterdamp nie, maar 'n klomp van daardie klein druppels of van klein stukkies ys. Niemand kan waterdamp sien nie, maar 'n wolk sien jy van ver af.
items.blok: Hoër op kondenseer die waterdamp
items.bron: Met Office, 'What are clouds and how do they form?': clouds are not water vapour, they are a large collection of tiny droplets, and higher, colder clouds are made of tiny ice crystals; Britannica, 'Cloud' (https://www.britannica.com/science/cloud-meteorology): 'any visible mass of water droplets, ice crystals, or a mixture of both'.

items.bewering: Waar dit koud genoeg is, vries 'n deel van die water in die siklus.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: NOAA, 'The water cycle': water is stored as ice in glaciers and sea ice, and falls as snow and hail; Met Office: cold, high clouds are made of ice. The lesson nowhere says that snow forms by freezing (most snow forms directly from vapour), so there is nothing false in this block's mention of snow.

items.bewering: Hael vorm in 'n donderstorm waar sterk wind die druppels hoog opdra. Die druppels vries daarbo tot ysklonte, en meer water vries laag vir laag daarop.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: NASA GPM FAQ, 'How does hail form?' (https://gpm.nasa.gov/resources/faq/how-does-hail-form): 'Hail forms when thunderstorm updrafts are strong enough to carry water droplets well above the freezing level. This freezing process forms a hailstone, which can grow as additional water freezes onto it.' NOAA NSSL Severe Weather 101, Hail (https://nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail), seen through search results because the page itself would not load: droplets freeze onto the stone on contact, and clear and cloudy layers form depending on how fast they freeze. 'Sterk wind' that carries upwards is a correct plain name for the updraft. The lesson rightly does not claim the disputed 'up and down many times' model.

items.bewering: 'n Ysklont val eers wanneer dit te swaar is vir die wind.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: NASA GPM FAQ, 'How does hail form?': 'Eventually, the hailstone becomes too heavy for the updrafts to support it and it falls to the ground.' NOAA NSSL forecasting page (https://nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/forecasting), seen through search results: hail falls when the updraft can no longer hold up its weight. That also covers an updraft that weakens, because the stone is then too heavy for the wind that is left.

items.bewering: Op hoë berge soos die Drakensberg kan sneeu en ys in die winter lê.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: SAnews (government news agency, https://www.sanews.gov.za/node/83103), July 2026: the South African Weather Service forecast snow on mountain peaks and singled out the Drakensberg; SABC News (https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/snow-blankets-drakensberg-peaks-as-temperatures-plunge/): SAWS reported snow on the southern Drakensberg peaks in July 2023; TimesLIVE, 10 August 2026: snow covered parts of the Drakensberg. A South African source on a South African claim. 'kan' is right, because it does not snow there every winter or for the whole winter.

items.bewering: Daardie sneeu en ys smelt weer wanneer dit warmer word. Die water loop dan by die berge af na die riviere toe.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: USGS, 'Snowmelt Runoff and the Water Cycle' (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/snowmelt-runoff-and-water-cycle): snowpacks melt in the warm season and release water into rivers; NOAA GML: liquid water forms when winter ice and snow melt and runs downhill under gravity.

items.bewering: Die klein druppels word groter en val as reën uit die wolk.
items.blok: Die siklus begin van voor af
items.bron: NOAA education activity (https://noaa.gov/node/10393): cloud droplets collide and merge into larger drops, which fall; University of Hawai'i atmospheric science text (https://pressbooks-dev.oer.hawaii.edu/atmo/chapter/chapter-7-precipitation-processes/): collision and merging is the main rain process in warm clouds. In many clouds rain starts as ice that melts on the way down, but the lesson says nothing against that, so the simple version holds.

items.bewering: Swaartekrag trek die reën af, en die water loop oor die land. Riviere dra die water terug see toe.
items.blok: Die siklus begin van voor af
items.bron: NASA GPM 'Exploring the Water Cycle' teacher's guide: gravity makes precipitation fall from clouds and water flow downward over the land; NOAA GML: runoff flows downhill through streams and rivers and some eventually reaches the oceans; USGS Water Science School kids' page (https://water.usgs.gov/edu/gallery/watercyclekids/runoff-beg.html): rivers flow on until they empty into the oceans.

items.bewering: Die reën wat val en die water in 'n rivier is albei 'n vloeistof. In hierdie stappe beweeg die water, maar dit verander nie van toestand nie.
items.blok: Die siklus begin van voor af
items.bron: Britannica, 'Phase change': rain and river water are liquid water, and falling and flowing are movement, not a phase change. The lesson's own earlier statement that rivers lose some water to evaporation does not clash with this, because it speaks of the falling and flowing steps themselves.

items.bewering: By die see verhit die son die water weer, en die siklus begin oor. Dieselfde water word oor en oor gebruik, en dit verdwyn nie.
items.blok: Die siklus begin van voor af
items.bron: USGS Afrikaans, 'Die Hidrologiese Siklus' (https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/die-hidrologiese-siklus-water-cycle-afrikaans): the water 'was nog altyd hier en is deel van die natuurlike watersiklus'; Washington State University, 'Ask Dr. Universe' (https://archive.news.wsu.edu/?p=147400): Earth's water is the same water that has been here for billions of years, and only a tiny amount has escaped into space. 'verdwyn nie' is true for any amount that matters.

items.bewering: Verdamp: die son verhit die see en die riviere, en 'n deel van daardie water word waterdamp.
items.blok: Vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle'; NOAA Ocean Today. Checked against the study text and the other three list items as one set: the four items agree with each other and with the study text.

items.bewering: Kondenseer: die waterdamp koel hoër op af en word weer klein druppels water.
items.blok: Vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: Met Office, 'What are clouds and how do they form?'; USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle'.

items.bewering: Vries: druppels vries hoog in 'n donderstorm en groei laag vir laag tot hael.
items.blok: Vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: NASA GPM FAQ, 'How does hail form?'; NOAA NSSL Severe Weather 101, Hail (through search results). Hail is a correct example of freezing. The list gives it as an example and does not say it is the only kind of freezing.

items.bewering: Smelt: sneeu en ys op hoë berge smelt wanneer dit warmer word.
items.blok: Vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: USGS, 'Snowmelt Runoff and the Water Cycle'; SAWS reports of snow in the Drakensberg (SAnews, SABC News, above).

items.bewering: watersiklus: Dieselfde water se pad tussen die see, die lug en die land.
items.blok: begrip: watersiklus
items.bron: NOAA, 'The water cycle'; USGS, 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle'. Read on its own, and also checked as a picture: 'pad' (a road or path) between the three places is correct, and it does not claim that every drop takes the same route. Most water evaporated from the sea falls straight back into the sea (USGS: only about 10% goes to land), which a road between three places allows. NOAA calls the simple circular model useful though incomplete. The picture holds at Grade 4.

items.bewering: swaartekrag: Die krag wat alles na die aarde toe aftrek.
items.blok: begrip: swaartekrag
items.bron: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, 'Ask an Explainer' (https://howthingsfly.si.edu/ask-an-explainer/what-gravity-7th-grade-words-and-understanding): gravity is a force that pulls you towards the Earth or any other mass. Read on its own: correct for Earth's gravity, which is what the lesson means. The fact that all masses attract one another is left out, and that is a simplification, not a falsehood.

items.bewering: waterdamp: Water in die vorm van 'n gas wat niemand kan sien nie.
items.blok: begrip: waterdamp
items.bron: Met Office, 'What are clouds and how do they form?': water vapour is invisible; USGS glossary: evaporation turns liquid water into a gas, water vapour. Correct read on its own.

items.bewering: wolk: Baie klein druppels water of stukkies ys wat saam hoog in die lug hang.
items.blok: begrip: wolk
items.bron: Britannica, 'Cloud' (https://www.britannica.com/science/cloud-meteorology): 'any visible mass of water droplets, ice crystals, or a mixture of both that is suspended in the air, usually at a considerable height'. Read on its own: correct. Fog is a cloud at ground level (Britannica, 'Fog'), but that is the exception to Britannica's 'usually', and the lesson does not mention fog.

items.bewering: smelt: Wanneer 'n vaste stof warm word en in 'n vloeistof verander.
items.blok: begrip: smelt
items.bron: Britannica, 'Phase change': melting is 'the transition from solid to liquid, as when ice warms and becomes liquid water'. Read on its own: correct.

items.bewering: verdamp: Wanneer 'n vloeistof in 'n gas verander. Dit gebeur vinniger wanneer die vloeistof warmer is.
items.blok: begrip: verdamp
items.bron: USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': evaporation changes liquid to gas and is much slower near freezing point than near boiling point; USGS circular: the rate varies with the water's temperature. Read on its own: correct, and it does not depend on the study block.

items.bewering: kondenseer: Wanneer 'n gas afkoel en weer in 'n vloeistof verander.
items.blok: begrip: kondenseer
items.bron: Britannica, 'Phase change': condensation is the change from gas to liquid, and it gives off energy, which is cooling. Read on its own: 'weer' assumes the gas was once a liquid. That is true for water vapour and kettle steam, the only gases a Grade 4 learner meets here, so it is not false in this lesson. Recorded because the entry was read on its own, as asked.

items.bewering: vries: Wanneer 'n vloeistof afkoel en in 'n vaste stof verander.
items.blok: begrip: vries
items.bron: Britannica, 'Freezing' (https://www.britannica.com/science/freezing-phase-change) and 'Phase change': freezing is liquid changing to solid, and it gives off heat. Read on its own: correct.

opsomming: Elke bewering is waar volgens NOAA, NASA, USGS, die Met Office, Britannica en Suid-Afrikaanse Weerdiens-berigte; die les bevat geen oortreffende trappe nie, en die twee beelde (die 'pad' van die water en die warm lug wat die water 'dra') hou, met die een voorbehoud wat 'n mens moet weet: die meeste water wat uit die see verdamp, reën terug in die see, en die les gee die eenvoudige land-roete sonder om te se dat elke druppel dit volg.
